comment: The draft appropriately favours assistive AI under meaningful human oversight, but oversight is described principally as a design characteristic. For outputs that require human review, oversight may become ineffective when output volume or complexity exceeds available review capacity, even though the system continues to be labelled assistive.

public.text: The draft appropriately favours assistive AI under meaningful human oversight, but oversight is described principally as a design characteristic. For outputs that require human review, oversight may become ineffective when output volume or complexity exceeds available review capacity, even though the system continues to be labelled assistive.
public.suggestedRevision: State that each deployment should define an operational oversight model proportionate to risk: which outputs require full review, sampling, exception review or escalation; the human capacity and competence required; and monitored thresholds indicating that oversight is no longer effective. A threshold breach should trigger re-evaluation of the deployment and its controls.
